chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ayoub ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So Allah saved him from the evil of what they planned.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But, they had extended (their hands) upon him, and killed him, but do you know what He saved him (from)? He saved him from their strife in his Religion.'

key_terms.يَفْتِنُوهُ: They would test/try him (to make him lose faith)

ai.seo_question: What did Allah save Prophet Yusuf from according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that divine protection for Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) was not merely physical preservation from the pit, but the preservation of his spiritual integrity and faith from the corruption of his brothers' schemes. This interpretation highlights a key Shia theological principle: the ultimate 'evil' (sayyi'at) is often the loss of din (religion/faith) rather than bodily harm, emphasizing that Allah safeguards the believer's inner conviction even amidst external trials.
